answer: Quartz-Ledger Entry Tax. Each new identity must post a small, non-refundable fee plus a fixed delay before its first transaction clears; the delay is drawn from a public randomness beacon, so batch-registering clones gains nothing. Honest agents amortize the fee across many legitimate actions. An attacker cloning N identities pays N fees and N delays, while a single honest identity pays once.
